correctness.rationale: The six vertices, eighteen directed arcs, no-cycle condition and all simplicial faces are explicitly enumerated by two independent exhaustive tests on 2^18 masks, yielding 714 nonempty faces. Exactly 336 distinct Hasse pairs admit a complete 714-vertex acyclicity topological sorting across 2376 incidences; critical cells occur 1,5,24,12 times in dimensions 0,2,3,4. Exact signed integer unit-pivot chain reduction gives a 5-by-24 degree-three differential with a 5-by-5 determinant-one minor, and identically zero 24-by-12 degree-four differential. Hurewicz maps for wedges of 2- and 3-spheres classify these attaching maps and permit five primitive cancellations, leaving 19 three-spheres and 12 four-spheres. Independent direct mod-two simplicial ranks (17,91,173,60) corroborate but are not substituted for the integral proof. The finite certificate, standard-library checker and recorded actual successful output are embedded.

originality.rationale: No covering statement was found in six targeted published-finding corpus queries, accessible own claims, or full primary texts on multipath and cycle-free chessboard complexes. The source on complete bipartite digraphs treats one-way orientations; Omega_6 treats the full complete bidirected digraph. Adjacent K_{2,n}/K_{3,4} results do not imply the present K_{3,3} result. A known universal top-degree Hamiltonian-cycle statement implies 12 top homology generators but neither 19 third-dimensional generators nor the integral homotopy splitting. Residual risk is an unindexed equivalent finite computation.

value.rationale: The balanced complete bipartite graph K_{3,3} is a canonical six-vertex cubic graph and a natural missing small case for bidirected multipath topology. Unlike a one-way orientation, the two-way arcs create directed cycles and a nonpure 714-face complex with facets in dimensions three and four. The exact integral homotopy classification and 19 previously unaccounted lower-degree spheres are informative for comparison with neighboring bidirected K_{2,n} and K_{3,4} results and for future parameter-family investigations, independent of any theorem for all sizes. The result is a natural full classification, not a routine arithmetic variant or arbitrary graph slice.
